21 . There are a variety of other statements in the New Testament that contributed to a negative depiction of
anger. Some examples are 1 Tim 2:8 where it was taught that prayers are to be offered in the Christian
assemblies "without anger or quarreling." Paul's teaching that love is "not irritable or resentful" in 1
Cor 13:5. Fathers are not to "provoke their children to anger" in their parenting (Eph 6:14) and believers in
general are warned to not "become conceited, provoking one another, envying one another" (Gal 5:26).
